# Held vendor submissions

Submissions that arrived through `/submit-tool.html` (FormSubmit → `aitoolsessentials@gmail.com`)
and are **not published**. Each was reviewed independently and placed on hold pending
verification. A verification request was sent in almost every case; where the vendor publishes no
reachable address, the row says so explicitly — a bounced or unsendable request is **not** a request
on file. Hold means "not rejected", not "forgotten".

Rule: do not re-send a verification request for an entry that is already listed here with a
sent date, and do not publish a held tool until the vendor answers the outstanding questions.

- **2026-11-24 01:12 PST (mail 2026-11-24 08:43 UTC, INBOX msg 324) — Banana Pro AI (`bananaproai.app`) HELD on the three dimensions the operator's standing instruction names (ownership, jurisdiction, pricing); one specific request sent, nothing seeded, nothing deployed. The lesson is that a site can clear every gate in `references/hold-vs-publish-decisions.md` and still not be listable, because the operator's own rule is stricter than the reference on three named dimensions.** The product is real, large and priced: 1,079 sitemap URLs, a `/models` directory reselling Google, OpenAI, Tencent and Black Forest Labs models by name, an `/llms.txt`, five locales, and a ladder that reconciles to the cent on every surface (monthly $9.90/$19.90/$39.90 for 500/2,000/6,000 credits; annual $58.80/$118.80/$238.80 = exactly 50% off; annual allowances exactly 12× the monthly ones; "cost per 100 credits" re-deriving on each card and repeated in the JSON-LD `OfferCatalog` and in the shipped plan config). It also has two things this ledger rarely gets to credit: a retention section that states the truth plainly (no automatic expiry for uploaded or generated objects; Delete in My Creations soft-deletes the task record without removing the stored object or provider copies), and no advertised-but-disabled namesake model (zero "coming soon" strings on any model page — the opposite of `seedream55ai`). **So the hold is not a legitimacy doubt, and the row says so in those words.** Three items block, and they are the three the cron instruction names: **(1) ownership** — no company, operator, data controller, postal address or entity anywhere, and the operator runs at least one other brand; **(2) jurisdiction** — the governing-law clause is circular ("the laws of the jurisdiction where bananaproai.app operates") and disputes go to "binding arbitration per applicable regulations" with no forum; **(3) pricing** — `/pricing` advertises "30-day money back" while the Terms say "All purchases are considered final and non-refundable except where legally mandated", with no refund page at any path. The legal set is also the pre-domain kind: both pages are headed "for **Nano Banana Pro**" and dated **Oct 24, 2025**, 66 days before the domain's **2025-12-29** registration, with no "last updated" element and no processor named as a company. **Method notes worth reusing.** (1) **A subdomain can be the undisclosed analytics tell** — the privacy policy names no vendor at all, yet a live session requested `https://p.bananaproai.app/api/event` alongside GA4; read `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` for same-site subdomains, not only third-party hosts, before writing "the policy names no analytics" or "only a counter runs". (2) **Google Ads tags show up in `rmkt`/`ccm`, and that is the finding** — the IDs `AW-17874774338` (Ads) and `G-6V7V7F1J4L` (GA4) both load *on the privacy policy page itself*, followed by `googleads.g.doubleclick.net/pagead/viewthroughconversion`, `google.com/rmkt/collect` and `google.com/ccm/collect`; that is conversion and remarketing tagging on the page making the privacy promise, which the generic phrase "GA4 loads" would have flattened. (3) **Consent-mode default is readable from the `dataLayer` before any click** — the first entry here is `consent default` granting `ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization` and `analytics_storage` all as `granted`, and on a cleared profile the site writes `localStorage.nbp_cookie_consent` = `{"necessary":true,"analytics":true,"marketing":true}` on first load with **no banner rendered for that visitor** (no cookie/consent string in the DOM after hydration). **CORRECTED 2026-11-24 (same day, while vetting `poseloop.app`, which ships the byte-identical script): a banner does exist — it is gated on the server-set `x-user-region` cookie and renders `Accept all / Reject all / Customize` only for `region=EU` or no region cookie.** Re-tested live on a cleared profile: `region=EU` → banner present, record unwritten; `region=OTHER` → no banner and the all-true record written on first load. Grade this "a geo branch standing in for a choice" rather than "no control at all", and set the region cookie explicitly to see both branches before believing a banner exists or does not. (4) **The per-visit countdown is one localStorage read away** — `promo_countdown_start` holds a fresh timestamp on each visit, which is what makes "ONLY 32 SPOTS LEFT" a permanent offer rather than a sale, and it is a one-line check.
